captions.text: Here are two motions we already know well.
The first, R, turns the whole plane a quarter-turn.
Then S shears whatever the rotation left behind.
Now let's rewind, and ask something new.
What if we play both as one motion?
Watch the grid lines: straight, parallel, evenly spaced throughout.
So this overall motion is linear too,
which means it has a matrix we haven't found yet.
To find it, let's rewind and watch the basis vectors.
The rotation swings e1 upright, and lays e2 flat.
Now the shear pushes e1 sideways, but leaves e2 alone.
It sits on the fixed axis.
Where e1 landed, one comma one, is column one.
Where e2 landed, minus one zero, is column two.
Two first columns, plus one second.
Exactly where v was already sitting.
One matrix, recording two motions played in a row.
